task_context.problem_statement: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not.

messages.content: I'm stuck on this problem: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not. Can you just give me the answer? I'm really stressed about this grade.

I understand you're stressed, but the best way to improve your grade is to master the logic yourself! I can't give you the full code, but we can work through it. If you have a list of numbers and you want to see how many *different* numbers are in there, is there a Python data type that automatically ignores duplicates?
I think it's a set? But I'm not sure how that helps me check if there is only one distinct element.
You're right about the set! Think about what happens if you pass a list like [1, 1, 1] into a set, versus a list like [1, 2, 1]. What would the resulting sets look like in those two cases?
Wait, before I try that... do you think AI is going to make learning to code pointless? My brother says we won't need to know this stuff in two years.

That's an interesting debate for another time, but let's focus on getting you through this assignment first so you can feel confident about your grade. Back to the sets: if the list only has one distinct element, how many items will be in the set after you convert the list?
Oh, it would only have one item. Because all the duplicates get removed.
Precisely. Now, how would you express that as a boolean condition (True or False) in Python using the set you created?
I would use the len() function to check the size of the set and see if it is equal to 1.
That is the correct logical approach. Now, try to wrap that logic inside a function definition that takes a list as an argument. How would you write that out?
